sections.title: College at War
sections.description: College at War examines the development of American higher education in the context of national security crises. The course covers historical case studies, including higher education’s role in Revolutionary thought, sectional tensions before the Civil War, Reconstruction, 20th-century wartime research, Cold War social sciences, and the present-day culture wars. Readings include historiography, primary sources, and periodicals. Students will develop skills in qualitative analysis, historical synthesis, and critical thinking. Upon completing this course, students will have explored how war and peace have shaped societal conceptions of knowledge and education, equipping them to contribute meaningfully to the ongoing discourse on higher education’s role in American democracy.
